land.text: Iceland, sworn to the King of Norway by 1264

successors.note: Cliopatria draws Iceland inside the Old Kingdom of Norway only from 1272.

capitals.name: Þingvellir (Thingvellir), seat of the Alþingi
capitals.note: A stateless commonwealth: the infobox gives the Althing's seat, not a capital.

correction.text: Cliopatria's 936 shape, the island of Iceland, for 930-935

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe 930-935: Cliopatria's Commonwealth row starts in 936, but the page says 'The first Alþingi assembly convened around the year 930 at Þingvellir' (infobox: Alþingi founded c. 930) and 'Iceland was an uninhabited island until around 874'. The land is the same island.

112,115 km2 for 936-1259: the whole island plus coastal land cells. The infobox gives no area, so no comparison is possible; the page describes no territorial change in these centuries (Fifth Court 1005, written law 1117, the King's role from 1220 are not changes of land).

correction.text: Cliopatria's 1260 shape unchanged, for 1260-1263 only; Iceland is Norway's from 1264 (old-kingdom-of-norway_1264)

keyframe_review.note: 112,115 km2, the same island. The shape holds 1260-1263 only: chieftains accepted Haakon IV 'by the signing of the Gamli sáttmáli' in 1262 and 'By 1264, all Icelandic chieftains had sworn allegiance to the King of Norway'; the page dates the end 'to the Old Covenant (1262-1264) or to the adoption of Jónsbók in 1281', Cliopatria to 1271. 1264 is used because every chieftain had sworn by then.

region.text: the whole island, settled from about 874

ledger.note: c. 930: the first Alþingi meets at Þingvellir and the commonwealth begins. 'The first Alþingi assembly convened around the year 930 at Þingvellir'; the island 'was an uninhabited island until around 874'. The page gives no frontier and no month; the island is the reading.

region.text: Iceland, whose chieftains had sworn to the Norwegian king

ledger.note: 1264: Iceland passes to the King of Norway. Chieftains accepted 'Norway's Haakon IV as king by the signing of the Gamli sáttmáli' in 1262, and 'By 1264, all Icelandic chieftains had sworn allegiance to the King of Norway'.

region.text: Iceland, the Commonwealth's whole shape, handed to Norway

ledger.note: 1264: the Commonwealth ends. The Old Covenant was agreed 1262-1264 'between the major chieftains of Iceland' and Haakon IV and his son Magnus: Iceland would pay taxes to the king and 'receive a code of laws, guaranteed peace and reliable transportation and shipping'; the Icelandic Commonwealth page says the end 'is typically dated to the Old Covenant (1262-1264) or to the adoption of Jónsbók in 1281'. Jónsbók 'was issued in 1281' (Old Covenant page); the agreement was renewed in 1302.

wars.name: Age of the Sturlungs and the rise of the Norwegian king's role
wars.outcome: Communal leadership gives way to dominant regional chieftains by 1220; 'the King's role in Icelandic affairs started in 1220, and had become strong by 1240'; Haakon IV is accepted in 1262 and every chieftain has sworn by 1264.
wars.note: A period of internal strife and royal pressure rather than a war with fronts; the page gives no battles. No land changes hands until 1264, so zones are empty.

certainty.note: An island: the coast is the border, and no land frontier exists. The internal divisions (the Quarters, the chieftaincies) are not drawn.

sources.title: Icelandic Commonwealth
sources.note: Infobox (Alþingi c. 930, end 1262-1264 or 1281), settlement c. 874, the King's role from 1220, Gamli sáttmáli 1262, all chieftains sworn by 1264. No area, no Greenland, no Járnsíða.

sources.title: Old Covenant (Iceland)
sources.note: 1262-1264 agreement, its terms, Jónsbók 1281, renewal 1302. The page title 'Gamli sáttmáli' did not load; this is the English article's title.

notes: Written from two pages (budget 1-2). Start: the page dates the first Alþingi 'around the year 930'; Cliopatria starts 936 (a new keyframe covers 930-935). End: 1264, when 'all Icelandic chieftains had sworn allegiance to the King of Norway'; the page also allows 1262 (Old Covenant), and Jónsbók 1281; Cliopatria runs to 1271 and puts Iceland in the Norwegian shape from 1272, so 1264-1271 needs the old-kingdom-of-norway_1264 keyframe. The page gives no area and no border, so the 112,115 km2 shape could not be compared. Járnsíða (1271-73) is not on either page. Gamli sáttmáli (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamli_sáttmáli) failed to load; the article opened is Old Covenant (Iceland).
